extraction.name: PASTIS
extraction.description: PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series) is the first large-scale, publicly available satellite image time series dataset with both semantic and panoptic annotations. It is comprised of 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral Sentinel-2 images of shape 10×128×128, each containing between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019, for a total of over 2 billion pixels. The dataset spans over 4000 km2 across four different regions of France and includes semantic labels for 18 crop types plus background, as well as unique instance labels for parcels.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot; Loic Landrieu
extraction.citeAs: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot and Loic Landrieu. Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks. ICCV 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is composed of 2,433 square 128×128 patches with 10 spectral bands at 10 m resolution, obtained from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform. For each patch, all available acquisitions between September 2018 and November 2019 were stacked to form four-dimensional multi-spectral satellite image time series. The patches were selected from four Sentinel-2 tiles in different regions of metropolitan France, favoring patches with rare crop types to reduce class imbalance. Acquisitions with extensive cloud cover were automatically filtered by the satellite data provider THEIA, but the authors did not apply further cloud detection and kept the raw data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The temporal sampling is irregular because patches are observed a different number of times and at different intervals, due to the Sentinel-2 orbit schedule and the policy of Sentinel data providers not to process tile observations identified as covered by clouds for more than 90% of the tile surface. Some patches are still partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch are annotated with the void label.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-access Sentinel-2 satellite imagery gathered from THEIA, using Copernicus data, and annotations from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) produced by IGN.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sentinel-2 tiles were subdivided into square patches of size 1.28×1.28 km (128×128 pixels at 10 m/pixel), and 2,433 patches were selected, favoring rare crop types. The authors selected all spectral bands except atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10. Parcel extents were cropped along patch boundaries and bounding boxes modified accordingly. Parcels with more than 50% of their surface outside the patch were assigned the void label. Classes with at least 400 parcels and samples in at least 2 of the 4 Sentinel-2 tiles were retained, leading to an 18-class nomenclature.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of Sentinel-2 after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel. Acquisitions with extensive cloud cover were automatically filtered by THEIA. No further pre-processing or cloud detection was applied, and the raw data were released. For modeling, sequences of variable length were padded with all-zero images at the end of shorter sequences, and a padding mask was retained to prevent encoding padded values and to exclude them from temporal averages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each pixel is associated with a semantic label from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class. Each non-background pixel also has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. In total, 124,422 parcels are individualized, each with bounding box, pixel-precise mask, and crop type. The annotations were taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System, allowing retrieval of parcel extent and content as reported by farmers. Pixels not within any declared parcel are labeled as background. Parcels belonging to classes outside the 18-class nomenclature or with insufficient overlap with a selected patch are annotated with the void label.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%. Predicted parcels overlapping a void parcel with IoU greater than 0.5 are ignored by the metric rather than counted as false positives or true positives.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One semantic label and one instance label per pixel
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are from farmers' declarations in the French Land Parcel Identification System; no further annotator demographics are provided.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available at https://github.com/VSainteuf/pastis-benchmark. No updating timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policy are specified for the dataset itself.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that panoptic segmentation of agricultural parcels has major economic and environmental implications. Remote monitoring of agricultural parcels is necessary for fair allocation of agricultural subsidies and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. The authors also state that the economic and environmental stakes of panoptic segmentation of satellite image time series cannot be understated.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. The authors selected 2,433 patches favoring patches with rare crop types in order to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance. The dataset covers four regions of France and almost 1% of metropolitan French territory.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The temporal sampling is irregular, with sequences containing different numbers of acquisitions at uneven intervals. Close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. Some parcels are visually fragmented but annotated as a single instance. Parcels outside the selected nomenclature or mostly outside patch boundaries are assigned the void label. The dataset covers only four regions of France, and geographically consistent folds for evaluating spatial generalization are noted as out of scope of the paper.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is introduced for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on satellite image time series, and is also used for semantic segmentation benchmarking. It is split into 5 folds for cross-validation, with official train/validation/test partitions. The paper presents it as panoptic-ready and suitable for benchmarking semantic and panoptic segmentation methods on agricultural parcel monitoring.
